## What holds

Quota truth is the conditional update in `StorageStoreRepository::reserveBytes()` (`packages/core/src/Repositories/Drive/StorageStoreRepository.php:24–43`). For `delta > 0` the statement is `used_bytes = used_bytes + ?` only when `quota_bytes IS NULL` or `used_bytes + ? <= quota_bytes`, on `VaulterDatabase::connection()`. Zero rows refresh the storage and throw `QuotaExceededException`; the caller’s transaction rolls back. `delta <= 0` goes to `adjustUsedBytes()`, which clamps at 0. On PostgreSQL this is atomic under `READ COMMITTED`: the second updater blocks on the storage row and rechecks the `WHERE`. On MySQL the same statement is atomic, and `lockTreeShared()` already holds that row. On SQLite the single writer plus this `WHERE` is the quota gate. An exact boundary passes; one byte over matches zero rows.

`UploadFileAction::executeUpload()` (`packages/drive/src/Actions/UploadFileAction.php:79–148`) stages once, then opens `transaction(..., 3)`. The fast `assertWithinQuota()` runs only for a new file (`:87–89`). A revision skips it, so a stale in-memory head cannot reject a shrink. Inside the transaction the order is shared drive lock, destination or target node, file aggregate for a revision (`:107`), head size from `current_version_id` (`:108–112`), `reserveBytes` or `adjustUsedBytes` (`:114–118`), then `commitStaged` (`:125`). The required comment is at `:92`. A new file gets `version_no` 1. A revision gets `$file->version_count + 1` (`:216`) and `repointHead` writes that number (`:230`), not an in-memory increment. `FileVersionStoreRepository::nextVersionNo()` is gone. No `nextVersionNo` call remains in the supplied core or drive sources.

`CopyNodeAction` (`packages/drive/src/Actions/CopyNodeAction.php:69–100`) takes the shared drive lock, snapshots the subtree, locks those nodes and the destination in one `ORDER BY id` `FOR UPDATE`, copies that set, and calls `reserveBytes` once with the sum. Trashed children stay out of the copy (`whereNull('trashed_at')`), which matches the copy rule that trash is not duplicated. Quota failure rolls the whole copy back. The locked node is what is copied, so a stale caller sees the head that committed before the node lock: upload updates node size and file head before it releases that lock.

Lock levels on the PostgreSQL paths do not step backward. Upload and copy take drive, then nodes, then (upload revision) the file row, then the quota update, then CAS. `commitStaged` (`packages/media/src/Cas/BlobStore.php:48–67`) takes `cas:{scope_key}:{sha256}` before `findOrCreate` and promote, and it does not discard. `commit()` is stage, `commitStaged`, `discard` in `finally`. Promote stays outside SQL rollback. `FileUploaded`, `NodeVersionCommitted`, and `NodeCopied` implement `ShouldDispatchAfterCommit`. The byte counter is recorded after the upload transaction returns. `VaulterDatabase::transaction()` defaults to 3 attempts (`packages/core/src/Database/VaulterDatabase.php:34`), and upload and copy pass 3. Move, restore, and force-delete keep drive-then-nodes; force-delete still releases bytes only through `adjustUsedBytes`. `detach`/`attach` take no CAS lock, so force-delete does not take level 5 and then level 4.

`BlobStore::commitStaged` is on the contract and in `packages/core/tests/Arch/__snapshots__/public-api.txt`. The media class implements it. Changelog `[Unreleased]` records the method and the E2/AD21 fix. Both guides describe conditional quota, drive → nodes → file → quota → CAS, head deltas, the three-attempt reuse of the staged object, and the promote saga.

V02 places the two 8 MiB uploads under different parents, so the parent lock cannot hide a broken quota update. Both pre-checks see 10 MiB free; only the conditional update can leave one winner, `used_bytes` equal to that head, and one blob row. Reconcile is aimed at the winner’s key after its mtime is older than grace. V03’s upload race uses two different sizes, so `used_bytes == final head` fails if both deltas were taken from the original head. The second V03 test locks only the file row, with a 100 ms overlap and no node lock, and expects `{2, 3}`.

## Related observations

Inherited, MySQL and SQLite. `lockTreeShared()` locks the storage row, which is also the quota row, and it does that before node locks. PostgreSQL uses a shared advisory tree lock and only later updates the row. Both upload and copy take that MySQL row first, so they queue on it instead of inverting node and quota.

Inherited, same-level node locks. `RestoreNodeAction` locks the node and root, then locks the original parent. `RenameNodeAction` locks the node, then its parent. The tree lock is what keeps those from running beside a move. P1.6 does not add a lower level after a higher one there.

Introduced doc residue, low. `docs/guide/uploads.md` still describes assemble as `UploadFileAction` → `BlobStore::commit`, and the CAS diagram in `docs/guide/storage-and-blobs.md` still shows `commit()` as the only entry. The new sections above those paragraphs are the accurate contract. Repair by pointing the assemble steps and the diagram at `stage` → `commitStaged` → caller `discard`.

The raw OPUS V20 row still expects `x.pdf` and `x (2).pdf`. The item scope excludes `OnNameConflict::Rename` and requires one node plus `NodeNameConflictException`. The test follows the item scope.

The raw OPUS V02 line calls the loser’s blob an orphan. Quota now runs before promote, so the loser never inserts a blob row and never promotes. That is the item’s V02 assertion. A row-less object still appears only when promote happens and a later SQL failure rolls the row back. `commitStaged`’s rollback test keeps the temp file, recommits, and dedups. Reconcile deletes a key only when it has no blob row, is past grace, and still has no row under the CAS lock.

## Evidence and limits

Author evidence in this pass is core Pint and PHPStan, both exit 0, plus the negative controls: quota control exit 1 once, revision control exit 1 on all five runs. The supplied note matches the aggregate test: with the upload node lock still present, removing `FileStoreRepository::lockForUpdate` is what produces duplicate `(file_id, version_no)`. The positive PostgreSQL suite, the SQLite `QuotaReserveTest` run, and the media CAS run are not in this evidence. They were not re-executed here.

V21 checks ten iterations of move-into-F beside upload-into-F, an acyclic tree, and `used_bytes` equal to the sum of file head sizes. It does not record retry counts, so the OPUS “at most one retry” bound is not measured. The lock sequence above is why a deadlock between those two should not form: each takes the tree lock before any node lock, and shared and exclusive advisory locks on that key queue.

`TusConcurrentPatchTest.php`, `ResolvesVaulterConnection`, and `CommitUploadAction` were not in the source bundle. Direct uploads stage outside any transaction. `UploadSessionManager::commitAssembled()` already holds the session row across the commit callable, which is the existing sweeper barrier. The inner upload retry still reuses one staged object. An assembled stream is seekable, and `Sha256ContentStore::stage()` rewinds seekable streams.

Concurrency tests use `DatabaseMigrations`, not `RefreshDatabase` (`packages/drive/tests/Pest.php`). `ForkRace` skips unless the driver is PostgreSQL, refuses a database name that does not end in `_test`, and gives each child its own connection. SQLite coverage of this item is `QuotaReserveTest`: unlimited quota, exact boundary, one byte over with `used_bytes` unchanged, zero and negative release, subtree copy over quota with no new rows, stale revision head, and stale copy head.
